text:
mia: Heads up — big latency spike in eu-west serving cluster, started 08:12Z. p95 jumped to ~1.2s and queues on gpu-pool-eu-01 are growing. Seeing MIG preemptions in kube events. Can we shift traffic while we triage?

arjun: Copy. Are we doing a canary or an atomic shift?

lee: Canary preferred normally but backlog doubling in 10m. If we can lower DNS TTL and move ~60% ASAP that buys time.

sam: Agree with lower TTL + weight move. Note: we should exclude Dedicated customers from the shift (they're pinned to eu-west). Only public-hosted routes.

opsbot: Alert from node-monitor: eu-west-nic-2 flap detected x3 in 6m, multiple Pods restarted due to device timeouts. Suggest network flaps affecting MIG VM stability.

arjun: I'll prepare gslb weight update and TTL change. Plan: set gslb weight eu-west -> 0.4, us-east -> 0.6, set DNS TTL 30s, and temporarily route burst traffic to quantized model variants in us-east to reduce GPU memory pressure.

mia: Sounds good. Also notify infra to stop rolling any maintenance in eu-west.

sam: Command block — what I'll run from ops jumpbox: 

```
# lower DNS TTL
gslbctl set-zone-ttl eu-west 30
# adjust weights
gslbctl update-pool-weights public-serving --weights eu-west=0.4,us-east=0.6
# pin dedicated routes
gslbctl set-route-exemption --route dedicated --zone eu-west
```

Please validate before apply.

lee: If we do weight shift, also bump min-replicas in us-east serving pool to avoid cold starts: 
```
kubectl patch hpa us-east-serving --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":5}}'
```

arjun: Applying steps now. Will push weight change then TTL.

opsbot: Executing step: drain-safeguard check passed. No active maintenance flags.

deploy-bot: gslbctl update accepted, transaction id tx-2026-11-07-001.

arjun: TTL lowered to 30s and weights updated. Monitoring convergence.

mia: Monitoring dashboards — p95 globally dropped to 620ms within 90s, eu-west queue length down 65%. Good.

lee: us-east autoscaler spun up 3 extra nodes to reach minReplicas=5, no OOMs observed.

sam: Note: egress/latency tradeoff — moving 60% to us-east will add ~12% egress for this window. Logging cost impact in the incident ticket.

opsbot: infra event: eu-west switch fabric flaps correlated with power maintenance at colo. Engineering alerted colo provider.

mia: Ok, keep public traffic on the new weights while we confirm hardware. On-call, keep watch for model errors — if we see >1% 5xx we fall back to local quantized variants in eu-west.

arjun: Opening incident: INC-2026-3882, attached logs and gslb tx id. Adding root-cause tag: network-flap.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step executed: lowered global DNS TTL to 30s. Next step: wait 30m and re-evaluate before returning traffic.

lee: After 20m — eu-west still shows intermittent MIG preemption but below threshold. We should keep shifted until colo confirms no additional flaps.

mia: I'll keep monitoring. Can someone capture the precise command output from gslbctl for the record?

arjun: Pasted output: 
```
$ gslbctl get-pool-status public-serving
pool: public-serving
  eu-west: weight=0.4 status=active  healthy=92/100
  us-east: weight=0.6 status=active  healthy=99/100
TTL: 30s
transaction: tx-2026-11-07-001
```

sam: Filing quick postmortem note: cost delta estimate for 2h window ~+$180 due to cross-region egress and extra node spin-up. Will include in incident doc.

opsbot: colo provider update: maintenance crew reports one switch had a failing PSU, replacement in progress. Expected resolution 2h.

mia: Good. We'll keep weights as-is until provider confirms. If flapping resumes we prepare atomic evacuate (set eu-west weight=0.0) with rollback plan.

arjun: Acknowledged. I'll script an atomic flip command if needed but prefer staged. Script: 
```
# emergency evacuate (if requested)
gslbctl update-pool-weights public-serving --weights eu-west=0.0,us-east=1.0 && gslbctl set-zone-ttl eu-west 10
```

lee: Confirmed monitoring playbook in place. Alerts adjusted to notify on >3% request errors in 5m window.

mia: Thanks all — incident mode: partial traffic shift in effect, triage ongoing. I'll update when colo confirms PSU replacement or if we need to escalate to full evacuate. :thumbsup:

sre-runbook-bot: Note appended to INC-2026-3882: actions performed: lowered ttl, adjusted gslb weights, bumped us-east minReplicas, pinned dedicated routes.

sam: Closing loop for now — keeping dedicated customers exempt minimized blast radius. Good call.

opsbot: Event update at 09:45Z — colo reports PSU swapped, no further flaps in 15m. Recommend returning 20% of traffic in stages.

mia: Let's stage return: eu-west -> 0.6, us-east -> 0.4, TTL 30s, wait 15m. If stable then return to normal weights after 1h.

arjun: Applying staged return now.

deploy-bot: gslbctl update accepted, transaction tx-2026-11-07-002.

lee: Metrics look stable after staged return, p95 within normal. eu-west MIG preemption rate near zero.

mia: Restoring normal weights in 1h if no regressions. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes.

arjun: Incident tagged Resolved-Provisional.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step executed: set monitoring to normal thresholds.

mia: Thanks team. Follow-up: add a play to pre-warm us-east pool for cross-region shifts to reduce spin-up cost next time.

sam: Will add to backlog and estimate cost impact.

opsbot: Incident closed to watchlist after 3h stable.

mia: End of thread.
